author: pereanub
title: Windows merge-queue build fails to clone submodules with SSL self-signed certificate error
signature: unable to access ssl certificate problem self signed certificate|Network

failed_jobs.name: Build / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: Clone OpenVINO step failed: git submodule fetch of thirdparty/ocl/cl_headers (KhronosGroup/OpenCL-Headers) and later thirdparty/onnx/onnx hit SSL 'self-signed certificate' errors after 3 retries

failed_jobs.name: ci/gha_overall_status_windows_debug
failed_jobs.symptom: Overall status check failed because the upstream Build job failed

key_errors: ##[error]fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/KhronosGroup/OpenCL-Headers.git/': SSL certificate problem: self-signed certificate
##[error]fatal: Fetched in submodule path 'thirdparty/ocl/cl_headers', but it did not contain 6fe718c31a45fe25151362a72ef041c3a1047cbd. Direct fetching of that commit failed.
##[error]fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/onnx/onnx.git/': SSL certificate problem: self-signed certificate
##[error]fatal: Fetched in submodule path 'thirdparty/onnx/onnx', but it did not contain 2bb50465112feca9003e1ed654d77f01ff1415ca. Direct fetching of that commit failed.
root_cause: The Windows merge-queue 'Clone OpenVINO' step performs a recursive/forced submodule update over HTTPS (git -c protocol.version=2 submodule update --init --force --depth=1 --recursive). While fetching several unrelated third-party submodules (KhronosGroup/OpenCL-Headers, then onnx/onnx) git reported 'SSL certificate problem: self-signed certificate', indicating the Windows runner's TLS trust chain (or an intercepting proxy/corporate SSL inspection appliance between the runner and github.com) presented a self-signed certificate instead of GitHub's real certificate. This is not caused by the PR's code changes (which only touch src/plugins/intel_npu/src/plugin/*) - it is an outbound network/TLS infrastructure issue on the Windows runner fleet. The step retried 3 times (14s, 10s backoff) and still failed on the third attempt, exhausting the checkout action's git-submodule retry budget.
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reliably reproducible outside the affected Windows runner's network path. To attempt reproduction: on the same Windows runner image, run `git -c protocol.version=2 submodule update --init --force --depth=1 --recursive` against a fresh clone of openvinotoolkit/openvino and observe whether TLS verification against github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com/objects for KhronosGroup/OpenCL-Headers.git succeeds.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'Build / Build' job (or re-queue the PR) - this looks like a transient runner/network TLS issue unrelated to the PR diff

If the failure recurs across multiple PRs/runs, escalate to the GitHub Actions runner infrastructure team to check for a misconfigured TLS-inspection proxy or expired/self-signed CA injected on the Windows runner image
Consider adding retry/backoff with a longer window or a fallback to protocol.version=1 for submodule fetches if this proves to be a persistent runner-image issue
Monitor for recurrence within the next 12 hours via the CI Doctor MQ pattern database (signature_hash abe11b87b263e6c2)
prevention_strategies: Track this failure signature in the repo-memory pattern database; if it recurs 3+ times within a 12-hour window, escalate via Teams to the CI infrastructure team to investigate the Windows runner image's TLS trust store or any SSL-inspecting network appliance. No code change is needed on the PR itself.
historical_context: A related but distinct SSL certificate failure (signature_hash d27ae006a3ab2b1f, 'Smart CI fails with SSL certificate verify failed self-signed certificate') was recorded once on 2026-08-12 for PR #37364, also a self-signed-certificate TLS failure but in the SmartCI job rather than during submodule cloning. This confirms self-signed-certificate TLS issues have intermittently affected this CI infrastructure before, supporting the Network/Infrastructure classification and transient nature of the current failure.
